newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina says capable of running Caltex oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina says capable of running Caltex oilfield.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina said on Wednesday it was capable of operating the Coastal Plain Pakanbaru (CPP) block which it will take over from PT Caltex Pacific Indonesia in 2001.
"Pertamina is capable of operating the CPP block when the production-sharing contract expires in 2001," Pertamina exploration director Priyambodo Mulyosudirjo told a news conference.
"It is not true that Indonesia's revenue will be reduced when the CPP block is taken over by Pertamina," he said.
His remarks came after a Tuesday statement by Caltex president Baihaki Hakim that he doubted if Pertamina could operate the block as it required high technology and a large amount of funding.
Caltex, jointly owned by Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc, on Tuesday appealed to the government to extend the CPP contract, which is due to expire in 2001.
A previous request to extend the 30-year contract had been rejected by Pertamina, which had said it wanted to operate the block that produces some 77,000 barrels-per-day of crude.
"We regret the Caltex president's statement that Pertamina will not be able to operate the field," Mulyosudirjo said.
"If the CPP is operated by Pertamina the government will earn more compared with when it was operated by Caltex because the government will get all of the earnings," he said.
Caltex operates the CPP on a 85-15 percent production-sharing basis in favour of Pertamina.
"Pertamina believes it can operate the block and it will give the benefits to the government. Therefore, Pertamina will not extend the CPP contract (with Caltex)," Mulyosudirjo said.
He said funding was not a problem and the company had experience in enhanced oil recovery projects.
"We are now making preparations to take over the block and to improve our expertise in enhanced oil recovery," he added.

Hakim said on Tuesday Caltex's total production in Indonesia was around 760,000 bpd, including 230,000 bpd from the Minas and 290,000 bpd from the Duri fields. That comprises about half of Indonesia's total crude production.
Pertamina currently operates several blocks, producing some 70,000 bpd of crude oil.
